# odyssey-083 — new renderings (table rows)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε περίφρων Πηνελόπεια (whole-line reply-formula, 17.162) | "Him then in turn addressed circumspect Penelope:" | "Then circumspect Penelope spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); built on the table's τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε and περίφρων Πηνελόπεια |
| τοῖσι δὲ καὶ μετέειπε Θεοκλύμενος θεοειδής (whole-line speech-introduction, 17.151) | "And among them spoke also Theoclymenus, godlike-in-form:" | "And Theoclymenus, godlike in form, spoke up among them as well:" | "addressed", "answered"; follows the table's τοῖσι δὲ καὶ μετέειπε γέρων ἥρως Ἐχένηος and θεοειδής |
| τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε συβώτης, ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν (whole-line speech-introduction, 17.184) | "and among them of speeches made-beginning the swineherd, chief of men:" | "The swineherd, chief of men, was the first to speak among them:" | "began the talk", "leader of men"; follows the table's τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε … rows and ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν |
| ὣς ἔφατ’ Ἀτρεΐδης, δουρικλειτὸς Μενέλαος (narrator's speech-closing formula, 17.147) | "So spoke the son of Atreus, Menelaus famed-for-the-spear." | "So spoke the son of Atreus, Menelaus, famed for his spear." | "So he spoke" (the bare ὣς φάτο is kept for an unnamed speaker); built on the table's ὣς φάτ’ Ἀθηναίη κούρη Διός, Ἀτρεΐδης used alone and δουρικλειτὸς Μενέλαος |
| ὣς φάτο, τῇ δ’ ἄρα θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ὄρινε (17.150; whole-line closing formula with its effect) | "So he spoke, and the heart in her breast he stirred." | "So he spoke, and he stirred the heart in her breast." | "moved", "troubled", "roused her spirit"; ὄρινε is "stirred" (the verb of ὀρίνω 'stir up') |
| ἀρισφαλής (17.196, ἀρισφαλέ’ … οὐδόν) | "very slippery" | "very slippery" | "treacherous", "unsafe" |
| οὐδός (17.196, in the sense 'ground underfoot'; οὐδός is 'threshold' in `l`) | "threshold" | "ground" (+ note: οὐδός is 'threshold', here probably the ground underfoot) | "path", "road" |
| θυμαρής (of a staff, 17.199) | "heart-fitting" | "a staff that suited him" | "pleasing", "dear", "comfortable" |
| βώτορες ἄνδρες (17.200) | "herdsmen" | "herdsmen" | "herders", "shepherds"; συβώτης stays "swineherd" |
| ὁμοκλή (17.189, ὁμοκλαί) | "rebukes" | "rebukes" | "threats", "reproaches"; follows "rebuke" for νεικέω |
| μέμβλωκε … ἦμαρ (17.190) | "has gone far, the greater part of the day" | "the day is already far spent" | "is nearly over", "has almost gone" |
| ῥυτήρ (17.187, ῥυτῆρα) | "protector" | "protector" | "guardian" (the table keeps it for φύλαξ), "keeper" (kept for ἐπιβώτωρ), "defender" |
| δείπνηστος (17.170) | "meal-time" | "time for the meal" | "dinner-time" (the table gives δεῖπνον "meal" and rules out "dinner"), "supper-time" (δόρπον keeps "supper"), "the hour of dinner" |
| βοῦν ἀγελαίην (17.181) | "a cow of the herd" | "a cow from the herd" | "a herd-cow", "an ox of the herd" |
| ἅρμασι κολλητοῖσιν (17.117) | "a well-joined chariot" (plural for one vehicle) | "a well-joined chariot" | "glued chariots", "well-fitted" |
| τὼ βήτην (17.200, dual) | "The two went" | "The two went on their way" | "They went" (loses the dual) |
